citing_name: Tarrant Appraisal Dist. v. Tarrant Reg'l Water Dist.
citing_court: Court of Appeals of Texas, Fort Worth
cited_name: Grand Prairie Hospital Authority v. Tarrant Appraisal District
explanation: Three-justice Fort Worth panel expressly overrules its own 1986 Grand Prairie holding as misreading Satterlee and the statute's text; en banc reconsideration denied, no intervening authority. Own knowledge: Texas en banc procedure (TRAP 41.2) and prior-panel norm existed.

Three-judge 2d DCA panel adopts a new pending-ordinance rule and 'recedes' from its own Pettersen to the extent of conflict, citing only pre-existing cases and a 'better rule'. Own knowledge: Fla. R. App. P. 9.331 en banc in force from January 1980.

Divided First District panel overrules its own Mathis on fairness grounds alone. But, from own knowledge, Ohio appellate districts had no established en banc procedure in 2004 (pre-McFadden 2008, App.R. 26(A)(2) 2010), so limb 4 fails.

Three-judge 3d DCA panel 'necessarily must recede' from its six-month-old Gonzalez statement that forcible entry is unavailable for residential tenancies, citing only its own statutory reading; it does not call the statement dicta. Own knowledge: en banc rule 9.331 existed.

citing_name: McHale v. Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance
cited_name: Travelers Indemnity Co. v. Skyway Marine, Inc.
explanation: Three-judge 3d DCA panel says its own Travelers Indemnity was 'incorrectly decided' and recedes from it and Alonso on burden of proving post-repair value; no intervening authority or statute. Own knowledge: en banc rule 9.331 existed in 1982.

Three-justice Fort Worth panel 'reconsidered' and disapproves its own 1994 Brown holding abolishing affirmative-link analysis, purely on re-reading Geesa, which predates Brown; no en banc marking. Own knowledge: Texas en banc procedure and prior-panel norm existed.

citing_name: In re Hoover, Bax & Slovacek, L.L.P.
explanation: El Paso 'Panel No. 1' says its own Cass misspoke in dismissing for want of jurisdiction and overrules it to that extent; only ground is the court's own error, though Cass is then held inapplicable. Own knowledge: Texas en banc procedure existed.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
cited_name: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania ex rel. Ricks v. Maroney
explanation: Third Circuit ordered the case resubmitted to the court en banc precisely to re-examine the Carey/Ricks certificate-timing rule, which it acknowledged bound all panels; the departure was by the full court, so the panel limb fails.

citing_name: State Farm Fire & Casualty Co. v. Sentry Indemnity Co.
cited_name: Federal Insurance Co. v. Insurance Co. of North America
explanation: Three-judge La. Third Circuit panel 'specifically overrule[d]' its own Federal Insurance holding as contrary to an Official Revision Comment; but, on my knowledge, Louisiana courts of appeal in 1975 followed jurisprudence constante with no binding prior-panel rule, so limb 4 fails.

Three-judge La. Fifth Circuit panel overruled its own Jacobs 'to the extent' of conflict, citing no intervening authority; text cannot show, and I cannot confirm from knowledge, that this circuit had a binding prior-panel rule in 2006.

citing_name: Washington Annapolis Hotel Co. v. Riddle
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia
explanation: Three-justice D.C. Circuit division expressly overruled the privilege theory of its own Brice v. Curtis, citing no intervening authority or full-court approval; on my knowledge the court could sit en banc by 1948, though its law-of-the-circuit rule was then less formal.

Three-judge Fourth DCA panel acknowledged conflict with its own Weymer holding and receded from it simply 'upon reconsideration', preferring the dissent; no en banc marking although, on my knowledge, Fla. R. App. P. 9.331 en banc procedure existed from 1980.

Three-judge Second DCA panel receded from its own Fulford identity-proof holding without en banc (available since 1980, my knowledge); Moorman is cited only for a general circumstantial-evidence principle, not as conflicting precedent, though that reading is debatable.

citing_name: Revell v. Morrison Supply Co., LLC
explanation: Three-justice Fort Worth panel held its own Kilpatrick revesting holding erroneous and overruled it, relying only on non-binding sister-court and Second Circuit criticism; Rule 41.2 en banc existed, and Texas panels are bound by prior panels (my knowledge; formalised in Mitschke 2022).

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
explanation: Three-judge D.C. Circuit division expressly overruled Hahn, Van Horne and Sinlao, preferring the later panel decision Wellman; no higher-court, statutory or full-court ground given. En banc and law-of-the-circuit existed in 1967 (own knowledge).

Three-judge Third DCA panel (one dissenting) receded in a footnote from its own Trujillo holding on emergency custody jurisdiction, citing no intervening authority; Fla. R. App. P. 9.331 en banc procedure existed since 1980 (own knowledge).

citing_name: Raphiel v. Morris Plan Industrial Bank of New York
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
explanation: Three-judge Second Circuit panel overruled In re Lesser simply as wrong; but in 1944 the Second Circuit did not sit en banc and had no settled prior-panel rule (own knowledge), so limb 4 fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
explanation: Tenth Circuit panel overruled Martinez so far as conflicting, footnoting Local Loan v. Hunt and a later panel case without stating a ground; in 1942 the circuit had no established en banc procedure or prior-panel rule (own knowledge).

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
explanation: Divided three-judge D.C. Circuit panel declared Caffrey, Biscayne and Lockwood 'should be overruled' as misreading earlier cases and decided contrary to them; no intervening authority. En banc was available by September 1948 (own knowledge; prior-panel rule then less settled).

First District three-judge panel expressly overruled Nadel under the Galatis stare decisis test, with no intervening authority; but Ohio appellate districts did not follow a prior-panel rule and App.R. 26 en banc came in 2010 (own knowledge), so limb 4 fails.

Second Circuit Louisiana three-judge panel overruled its own Parker v. Smith, following the Fourth Circuit's Shipman; but Louisiana courts of appeal, under jurisprudence constante, had no binding prior-panel rule in 1977 (own knowledge), so limb 4 fails.

Three-judge 3d DCA panel 'specifically recede[s]' from its own post-1973 Watson, citing only sister-district cases; no en banc, though Rule 9.331 existed from Jan 1980 (own knowledge). Statute change covers Layton, not Watson.

Same three-judge Kentucky panel calls Wilson distinguishable (no judgment/sentence of probation there) and overrules only 'any holding in conflict'; truncated Wilson text cannot show an actual holding was displaced. En banc rule SCR 1.030(7)(d) from own knowledge.

citing_court: Court of Criminal Appeals of Alabama
explanation: Woods overrules Phillips, but all five judges of the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals participated (the court sits as a whole; own knowledge), and it relied on the later Alabama Supreme Court decision Ex parte Sorsby.

citing_name: In the Interest of G. A. R.
explanation: Three-judge 4th DCA panel in July 1980 recedes from St. John's announced rule on anonymous tips, persuaded only by 2d DCA's Hetland; no higher or en banc authority, though en banc Rule 9.331 was available (own knowledge).

Three-judge 2d DCA panel in 1982 'necessarily recede[s]' from Olcott's remand proviso applying Pearce to resentencing; authorities cited predate Olcott, no en banc or dicta claim; en banc rule existed (own knowledge).

cited_name: Karl A. Kandell Associates, Inc. v. Urbanek
explanation: Zimbrick recedes from Urbanek and Tri-State, but eight 4th DCA judges participated (six concurring, two concurring in result), so the court sat en banc, not as a panel.

Three-judge 2d DCA panel recedes from Miles in 1973 on intervening Fifth Circuit constitutional rulings, but Florida DCAs had no en banc procedure until Rule 9.331 in 1980 (own knowledge), so limb 4 fails.
